# hoop_sidecar_service_account (Resource)

Lets sidecars authenticate with a token their platform issued, a Kubernetes projected service account token or a Google ID token, instead of a token the control plane issued per sidecar. A matching token reaches the sidecar `name_template` names, and the control plane creates that sidecar on its first handshake. Use `data.hoop_sidecar` to bind rules to a sidecar created this way. Needs an Enterprise license, checked at plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

# Every pod running the hoop-sidecar service account in any namespace of this
# GKE cluster reaches a sidecar named after its namespace, with no token to
# hand out. The helm chart sets HOOP_SIDECAR_IDENTITY_TYPE=kubernetes.
resource "hoop_sidecar_service_account" "gke_eu" {
  name            = "gke-eu"
  issuer          = "https://container.googleapis.com/v1/projects/my-project/locations/europe-west1/clusters/eu"
  audience        = "https://hoop.example.com"
  claim           = "sub"
  subject_pattern = "system:serviceaccount:*:hoop-sidecar"
  name_template   = "gke-eu-{1}"
}

# A Google service account on GCE, matched by email.
resource "hoop_sidecar_service_account" "gce" {
  name            = "gce-sidecars"
  issuer          = "https://accounts.google.com"
  audience        = "https://hoop.example.com"
  claim           = "email"
  subject_pattern = "sidecar-*@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  name_template   = "gce-{1}"

  # Sidecars an admin registered with a token may be adopted by this identity.
  adopt_existing_sidecars = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `audience` (String) The `aud` the tokens must carry: the control plane URL the sidecar uses. One organization owns each issuer and audience pair.
- `claim` (String) The claim matched against `subject_pattern`. `sub` for a Kubernetes service account; `email` for a Google service account, whose token must carry `email_verified`.
- `issuer` (String) The exact `iss` of the tokens. An https URL. The control plane fetches the signing keys through OIDC discovery unless `jwks` is set.
- `name` (String) A label for this mapping, unique in the organization.
- `name_template` (String) The name of the sidecar a matching token reaches. `{1}` is the text the `*` matched.
- `subject_pattern` (String) An exact value, or one with a single `*` that matches one or more characters, such as `system:serviceaccount:*:hoop-sidecar`. A bare `*` needs `allow_any_subject`.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing_sidecars` (Boolean) Lets a matching token reach a sidecar an admin registered with a token, when no identity is bound to it yet, and binds it. Without it such a token is refused.
- `allow_any_subject` (Boolean) Allows the bare `*` pattern, which admits every subject of the issuer.
- `jwks` (String) A static JWKS document for an issuer the control plane cannot reach. Omit it to use OIDC discovery on the issuer.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

terraform import hoop_sidecar_service_account.gke_eu 30ebf0cd-040e-4c89-9d6e-28f03f472a41
```
